Priyadarshan directed Khan in Billu (2009), a Red Chillies production remade from the Malayalam Katha Parayumpol, in which Khan plays the superstar Sahir Khan, who returns to a village and publicly honours his forgotten childhood friend, a poor barber played by Irrfan Khan. Variety called the film's climax, Khan's school speech, emotionally effective.

name: Sajid Nadiadwala
career_background: Grandson of the producer Abdul Karim Nadiadwala; assistant director to J. P. Dutta on Ghulami before founding Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment at 25.
debut: First production: Zulm Ki Hukumat (1992).
major_works: Jeet (1996); Judwaa (1997); Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000); Mujhse Shaadi Karogi (2004); Heyy Babyy (2007); Housefull (2010); Kick (2014, director); Baaghi (2016)
recurring_themes: Mainstream comedies and action films, often starring Salman Khan or Akshay Kumar.
historical_importance: A prolific commercial producer whose franchises include Housefull and Baaghi; won a debut-director award for Kick.
relationship_with_actor: Produced two films featuring Khan in brief appearances: a closing role in Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega and a song cameo in Heyy Babyy.
biography: Sajid Nadiadwala, born on 18 February 1966, is the grandson of Abdul Karim Nadiadwala, who moved to Mumbai from Nadiad in 1955 and produced hundreds of films. After graduating he worked as an assistant director to J. P. Dutta on Ghulami and as a production assistant in his uncle's company, then founded Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment at 25. His first production was Zulm Ki Hukumat (1992), and he brought Akshay Kumar and Suniel Shetty together in Waqt Hamara Hai (1993). He produced the Salman Khan hits Jeet (1996) and Judwaa (1997), followed by Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega (2000), in which Shah Rukh Khan makes a closing special appearance, and Mujhse Shaadi Karogi (2004). Khan also appears in a song in Sajid Khan's Heyy Babyy (2007), which Nadiadwala produced. His later films include Housefull (2010) and Baaghi (2016), and he won a debutant director award for Kick. His first wife, the actress Divya Bharti, Khan's co-star in Deewana, died in 1993.

name: Sandeep Chowta
career_background: Born in Ghana, raised in Nigeria and Bangalore; son of the Tulu author D. K. Chowta; head of Columbia Records in India and a core member of the group AO Music.
major_works: Aśoka (2001, score); Om Shanti Om (2007, score); Billu (2009, score); 12 Telugu films
historical_importance: AO Music albums crediting him have charted in the international top five.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Aśoka, Om Shanti Om and Billu.
biography: Sandeep Chowta, born in 1967 or 1968 in Ghana, grew up in Nigeria before moving to Bangalore; he is the son of D. K. Chowta, a Tulu author and businessman. He works mainly in Hindi and Telugu cinema, has composed music for 12 Telugu films, and heads Columbia Records in India. In 2003 he produced the anti-substance-abuse documentary Dead End, and since 2004 he has been a core member of the new-age group AO Music, whose albums have charted in the international top five. For Shah Rukh Khan he wrote the background scores of Santosh Sivan's Aśoka (2001), Farah Khan's Om Shanti Om (2007) and Priyadarshan's Billu (2009), while other composers wrote their songs.

name: Aadesh Shrivastava
career_background: Born in Katni; worked as a drummer for R. D. Burman and Rajesh Roshan before becoming a composer; married to the actress Vijayta Pandit, sister of Jatin–Lalit.
debut: First big break with Kanyadaan (1993), for which Lata Mangeshkar sang his first song.
major_works: Aao Pyaar Karen; Shastra; Bas Itna Sa Khwaab Hai (2001); Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001); Chalte Chalte (2003); Paheli (2005, score); Alag (2006); Raajneeti (2010, 'Mora Piya')
recurring_themes: Punjabi-inflected popular songs such as 'Shava Shava' and semi-classical numbers.
historical_importance: Composed music for over 100 Hindi films and was a judge on Sa Re Ga Ma Pa.
relationship_with_actor: Contributed songs to Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, composed the songs and score of Chalte Chalte, scored Paheli and composed Alag, in which Khan appears in a song.
biography: Aadesh Shrivastava (4 September 1964 – 5 September 2015) was born in Katni and worked as a drummer for composers including R. D. Burman and Rajesh Roshan before composing independently. His first break, Kanyadaan (1993), featured Lata Mangeshkar singing his first song; after further setbacks he found hits with Aao Pyaar Karen and Shastra. He sang popular songs including 'Sona Sona' and 'Shava Shava', judged Sa Re Ga Ma Pa, and made a short film on child prostitution, Sanaa; his semi-classical 'Mora Piya' from Raajneeti became popular. He composed for over 100 Hindi films, and he married Vijayta Pandit, sister of the duo Jatin–Lalit. For Shah Rukh Khan he contributed songs to Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001), composed songs and the score for Chalte Chalte (2003), wrote the background score for Paheli (2005) and composed Alag (2006), in which Khan appears in a song. He died of cancer a day after his 51st birthday.

name: Sajid–Wajid
career_background: Brothers Sajid Khan and Wajid Khan, sons of the tabla player Sharafat Ali Khan; their maternal grandfather Ustad Faiyyaz Ahmed Khan received the Padma Shri.
major_works: Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002); Kismat Konnection (2008, guest composition)
recurring_themes: Sufi-inflected Bollywood songs.
historical_importance: A leading Bollywood composer duo until Wajid Khan's death on 1 June 2020; Sajid Khan has since worked solo.
relationship_with_actor: Contributed songs to Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam and a guest composition to Kismat Konnection, which Khan narrates.
biography: Sajid–Wajid were the Bollywood composer duo of the brothers Sajid Khan and Wajid Khan, sons of the tabla player Sharafat Ali Khan and grandsons, through their mother, of the Padma Shri recipient Ustad Faiyyaz Ahmed Khan. Active from 1998, they also wrote lyrics and background scores, and Wajid Khan sang some of their songs. Wajid Khan died on 1 June 2020, after which Sajid Khan continued as a solo artist. Their connection to Shah Rukh Khan's films is limited: they were among the composers of Hum Tumhare Hain Sanam (2002) and provided a guest composition for Aziz Mirza's Kismat Konnection (2008), which Khan narrates.

name: Ismail Darbar
career_background: Film-score composer, instrumentalist, singer, violinist and music director.
major_works: Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999); Devdas (2002); Shakti: The Power (2002)
recurring_themes: Indian classical music in large-scale film soundtracks.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction (Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam); R. D. Burman Award (1999)
historical_importance: Composer of Sanjay Leela Bhansali's two landmark musicals of 1999–2002.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for Devdas, with Birju Maharaj, and for Shakti: The Power.
biography: Ismail Darbar is an Indian film composer, instrumentalist, singer and violinist, born in 1964, whose work draws heavily on Indian classical music. He won the R. D. Burman Award in 1999 and the National Film Award for Best Music Direction for Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999). He reunited with Bhansali for Devdas (2002), composing the songs with the Kathak master Birju Maharaj while Monty Sharma wrote the background score. Its songs, including 'Dola Re Dola', won Filmfare Awards for their singers and choreographer. The same year he composed Krishna Vamsi's Shakti: The Power, in which Shah Rukh Khan plays a supporting role, with Anu Malik adding a guest composition.

name: Monty Sharma
career_background: Born in Mumbai; trained from the age of five under his grandfather Pandit Ram Prasad Sharma; nephew of Pyarelal of Laxmikant–Pyarelal; a keyboard player from age sixteen, starting with Mr. India.
major_works: Devdas (2002, score); Silsiilay (2005, score); Black (2005, score); Saawariya (2007, music director); Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013, score); Gadar 2 (2023, score)
recurring_themes: Orchestral background scores, particularly for Sanjay Leela Bhansali.
historical_importance: Background composer for several Bhansali films.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Devdas and Silsiilay, which Khan narrates.
biography: Monty Sharma, born on 17 April 1970 in Mumbai, began learning music at five under his grandfather Pandit Ram Prasad Sharma and is the nephew of Pyarelal of the Laxmikant–Pyarelal duo. At sixteen he became a professional keyboard player with Laxmikant–Pyarelal on Mr. India, and he went on to work with R. D. Burman, Rajesh Roshan, Nadeem–Shravan, Jatin–Lalit and Ismail Darbar. As a background-score composer he is best known for Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Devdas (2002), Black (2005) and Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), and he was music director of Saawariya (2007). He has also judged STAR Voice of India 2. He scored two Shah Rukh Khan films: Devdas and Khalid Mohamed's anthology Silsiilay (2005), which Khan narrates.

name: Sanjay Leela Bhansali
career_background: Founded Bhansali Productions and later debuted as a music composer with Guzaarish.
debut: Khamoshi: The Musical (1996).
major_works: Khamoshi: The Musical (1996); Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999); Devdas (2002); Black (2005); Saawariya (2007); Guzaarish (2010); Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013); Bajirao Mastani (2015); Padmaavat (2018)
recurring_themes: Tragic romance and period drama.
creative_style: Opulent aesthetics and a strong musical vision.
major_awards: 7 National Film Awards; 13 Filmfare Awards; Padma Shri (2015); BAFTA nomination for Devdas (Best Film Not in the English Language)
historical_importance: One of Hindi cinema's foremost stylists; Devdas was the highest-grossing Indian film of 2002 and India's Academy Award submission.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan as the self-destructive lover in Devdas, which won Khan the Filmfare Award for Best Actor.
biography: Sanjay Leela Bhansali, born on 24 February 1963, is a filmmaker and composer known for his aesthetics and musical vision, particularly in period dramas. His honours include seven National Film Awards, thirteen Filmfare Awards, a BAFTA nomination and the Padma Shri (2015). After his debut, Khamoshi: The Musical (1996), he achieved critical and commercial success with the romantic dramas Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam (1999) and Devdas (2002). He won the National Film Award for Best Hindi Film for Black (2005); after the failures of Saawariya and Guzaarish he returned with Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), Bajirao Mastani (2015) and Padmaavat (2018). Devdas, his version of Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel, cast Shah Rukh Khan as the London-educated heir who abandons his childhood love Paro (Aishwarya Rai), turns to drink, finds refuge with the courtesan Chandramukhi (Madhuri Dixit) and dies at Paro's gates. Built on sets costing ₹200 million and premiered at Cannes, it was the highest-grossing Indian film of the year and India's Academy Award submission. It won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and swept the major Filmfare awards, including Best Actor for Khan, although Indian reviews of the lead performances were divided.

name: Nikkhil Advani
career_background: Assisted Saeed and Aziz Mirza on Naya Nukkad, co-wrote Iss Raat Ki Subah Nahin, and was assistant director to Karan Johar on Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham and to Aditya Chopra on Mohabbatein.
debut: Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003).
major_works: Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003)
creative_style: Emotionally driven drama in the Dharma Productions mould; Anupama Chopra described him as 'a distinctive voice'.
major_awards: Kal Ho Naa Ho won two National Film Awards and eight Filmfare Awards.
historical_importance: An assistant from Khan's biggest romances of the late 1990s who directed one of the most successful films of 2003.
relationship_with_actor: Assisted on three Khan films and made a guest appearance in Kuch Kuch Hota Hai before directing him as the dying Aman in Kal Ho Naa Ho.
biography: Nikkhil Advani, born Nikhil Suresh Advani on 28 April 1971 in Bombay, is a director, producer and screenwriter who co-founded the company Emmay Entertainment with his sister Monisha Advani and Madhu Bhojwani. He studied chemistry at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and started his career assisting Saeed and Aziz Mirza on the television series Naya Nukkad (1994), then co-wrote Iss Raat Ki Subah Nahin (1996). He was an assistant director to Karan Johar on Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998), in which he also appeared in the Neelam talk-show sequence, and on Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001), and to Aditya Chopra on Mohabbatein (2000), all starring Shah Rukh Khan. Advani made his directorial debut with Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), written by Johar and set in New York. Khan plays Aman, a cheerful neighbour secretly dying of a heart condition, who steers the woman he loves towards her best friend. The film was critically acclaimed, became the highest-grossing Hindi film of the year worldwide, and won two National Film Awards and eight Filmfare Awards.

name: Niranjan Iyengar
career_background: Born in Dombivali, Maharashtra; closely associated with Karan Johar; author of The Making of Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham... and host of the talk show Look Who's Talking with Niranjan on Zee Café.
major_works: Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003, dialogues); Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006); My Name Is Khan (2010); Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016, dialogues)
recurring_themes: Dialogue for relationship dramas.
historical_importance: A key writing collaborator on Dharma Productions' relationship dramas.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote dialogue or script material for four Khan films, all Karan Johar productions.
biography: Niranjan Iyengar, born in Dombivali, Maharashtra, is a screenwriter and lyricist particularly known for his work with Karan Johar. He wrote The Making of Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham..., a book on Johar's 2001 film, and hosts the talk show Look Who's Talking with Niranjan on Zee Café. His writing credits on Shah Rukh Khan's films are all Dharma Productions projects: the dialogues of Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), script contributions to Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006), co-writing credit on My Name Is Khan (2010) with Shibani Bathija, and the dialogues of Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016), in which Khan makes a cameo.

name: Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy
industry: Hindi; Tamil; Malayalam; Telugu; Marathi; English
career_background: Shankar Mahadevan, Ehsaan Noorani and Loy Mendonsa; Loy composed the title track for Khan's early television serial Fauji.
major_works: Dil Chahta Hai (2001); Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003); Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006); Don (2006); My Name Is Khan (2010); Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011); Don 2 (2011); Dil Dhadakne Do (2015)
recurring_themes: Rock, world and Indian classical fusion.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction and Filmfare Award for Best Music Director (Kal Ho Naa Ho); IIFA Awards; Padma Shri for Shankar Mahadevan (2019)
historical_importance: Called the 'Amar Akbar Anthony' of Hindi film music; over 50 soundtracks in five languages.
relationship_with_actor: Composed eight Khan films, including Kal Ho Naa Ho, Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, both Don films and My Name Is Khan; Loy's association with Khan dates back to Fauji.
biography: Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy is the trio of Shankar Mahadevan, Ehsaan Noorani and Loy Mendonsa, who have composed over 50 soundtracks in Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam, Telugu, Marathi and English and are often called the 'Amar Akbar Anthony' of Hindi film music. They are known for Dil Chahta Hai (2001), Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna (2006), My Name Is Khan (2010), Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011) and Dil Dhadakne Do (2015), and have won National Film Awards, Filmfare Awards and IIFA Awards; Shankar Mahadevan received the Padma Shri in 2019. Loy Mendonsa's link with Shah Rukh Khan predates films: he composed the title track for Khan's television serial Fauji. The trio's first collaboration with Karan Johar, Kal Ho Naa Ho, won them the National Film Award for Best Music Direction and the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director. They went on to compose Khan's Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna, Don, Heyy Babyy, Luck by Chance, My Name Is Khan and Don 2, and The Zoya Factor, which he narrates.

name: Gauri Khan
function: Producer (co-founder of Red Chillies Entertainment); interior designer
career_background: Interior designer who launched Gauri Khan Designs in 2013, opened the concept store The Design Cell in 2014 and an Experience Centre in Delhi in 2025.
major_works: Main Hoon Na (2004); Paheli (2005); Om Shanti Om (2007); My Name Is Khan (2010); Ra.One (2011); Chennai Express (2013); Happy New Year (2014); Dear Zindagi (2016); Jawan (2023); Dunki (2023)
historical_importance: Included in Fortune magazine's list of the '50 Most Powerful Women' in 2018.
relationship_with_actor: Married to Khan since 25 October 1991, after they met in Delhi in 1984; co-founder and joint managing director of Red Chillies and credited producer on 16 of his films.
biography: Gauri Khan, born on 8 October 1970, is a film producer and interior designer. She met Shah Rukh Khan in Delhi in 1984 and married him on 25 October 1991. With him she co-founded Red Chillies Entertainment, where she is joint managing director, and she has been the credited producer on 16 of his films, from Main Hoon Na (2004) and Paheli (2005) through Om Shanti Om, Billu, My Name Is Khan, Ra.One, Chennai Express, Happy New Year, Dilwale, Dear Zindagi, Raees, Jab Harry Met Sejal and Zero, to Jawan and Dunki (2023). She also produced the teen comedy Always Kabhi Kabhi (2011), in which Khan appears in a song. Alongside producing, she launched Gauri Khan Designs in 2013, opened the concept store The Design Cell in Worli in 2014 and an Experience Centre in Delhi in 2025. Fortune magazine named her one of its '50 Most Powerful Women' in 2018.

name: Red Chillies Entertainment
function: Production and distribution company founded by Shah Rukh Khan and Gauri Khan
career_background: Evolved from the defunct Dreamz Unlimited; based in Mumbai, with divisions for film and television production, distribution, visual effects (Red Chillies VFX), colour, television commercials and sports.
debut: First production: Main Hoon Na (2004); second: Paheli (2005).
major_works: Main Hoon Na (2004); Paheli (2005); Om Shanti Om (2007); Billu (2009); My Name Is Khan (2010); Ra.One (2011); Chennai Express (2013); Happy New Year (2014); Dilwale (2015); Dear Zindagi (2016); Raees (2017); Zero (2018); Badla (2019); Jawan (2023); Dunki (2023)
recurring_themes: Large-scale star vehicles for Khan and effects-heavy productions.
major_awards: Red Chillies VFX won Filmfare Awards for Best Special Effects for Om Shanti Om, Ra.One, Fan, Zero and Jawan; Paheli was India's Academy Award submission.
historical_importance: A multinational entertainment company with a major visual-effects division, a 26% stake in the operator of KidZania India, and links to the Kolkata Knight Riders through its CEO.
relationship_with_actor: Khan's own company, with Khan as managing director and Gauri Khan as joint managing director; it produced or co-produced 18 of his films and has acquired the rights to many of his 1990s films.
biography: Red Chillies Entertainment is the Mumbai-based entertainment company founded by Shah Rukh Khan and Gauri Khan out of their earlier partnership Dreamz Unlimited. Its article gives the founding year as 2002; Gauri Khan's article gives both 2001 and 2002. Its activities span development, production, marketing, distribution, licensing, merchandising and syndication, and it runs the visual-effects house Red Chillies VFX, a colour division and a television-commercials unit. It owns 26% of ImagiNation Edutainment, which runs KidZania India; Venky Mysore, also CEO of the Kolkata Knight Riders, became its CEO in 2013. Khan is managing director and Gauri Khan joint managing director. Its first production was Farah Khan's Main Hoon Na (2004), and its second, Paheli (2005), was India's Academy Award submission. Most of its films have starred Khan, including Om Shanti Om, My Name Is Khan, Ra.One, Chennai Express, Happy New Year, Dilwale, Raees, Zero, Jawan and Dunki, although it has also backed films without him, such as Badla (2019). The company has acquired the rights to many of Khan's earlier films, including Kabhi Haan Kabhi Naa, Anjaam, Ram Jaane, Yes Boss and One 2 Ka 4. Red Chillies VFX has repeatedly won the Filmfare Award for Best Special Effects.

name: UTV Motion Pictures
career_background: The feature-film unit of UTV Software Communications, founded in 1996 by Ronnie and Zarina Screwvala; known as Disney UTV in 2012–2013.
major_works: Swades (2004); Chennai Express (2013); Jagga Jasoos (2017)
historical_importance: One of India's leading film studios and a distributor of Disney films in India; it shut its Hindi film production in July 2017.
relationship_with_actor: Co-produced Swades with Ashutosh Gowariker and produced and distributed Chennai Express with Red Chillies Entertainment.
biography: UTV Motion Pictures was the feature-film unit of UTV Software Communications, founded in 1996 by Ronnie Screwvala and Zarina Screwvala. It became one of India's leading film studios and one of the largest production studios in South Asia, with activities across development, production, marketing, distribution, licensing, merchandising and syndication. It partnered with Hollywood studios including 20th Century Studios, Walt Disney Pictures and Sony Pictures, distributed Disney's films in India, and operated as Disney UTV in 2012–2013. In July 2017, shortly after Jagga Jasoos, it stopped Hindi film production. With Shah Rukh Khan, UTV co-produced Ashutosh Gowariker's Swades (2004), which failed commercially but became a cult classic. It also produced and distributed Rohit Shetty's Chennai Express (2013) with Red Chillies Entertainment; Screwvala and Siddharth Roy Kapur are among its credited producers, and it became the highest-grossing Bollywood film at the time.

name: Himesh Reshammiya
debut: Composer debut Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998); acting debut Aap Kaa Surroor (2007).
major_works: Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998); Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005); Silsiilay (2005); 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne'; Aap Kaa Surroor (2007)
recurring_themes: Dance-pop, disco, Sufi-inflected Bollywood songs.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer (2006, 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne'); IIFA and Zee Cine playback awards
historical_importance: Over 1,300 credited songs; ranked 22nd in Bloomberg's list of the world's most influential pop stars in 2025, the only Indian on it.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye and Silsiilay, both 2005 films in which Khan makes brief appearances.
biography: Himesh Reshammiya, born on 23 July 1973, is a playback singer, music director, songwriter, producer and actor with over 1,300 credited songs. He began as a composer with Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya (1998) and later turned to singing; 'Aashiq Banaya Aapne' won him the Filmfare, IIFA and Zee Cine awards for best male playback singer. He made his acting debut in Aap Kaa Surroor (2007). In August 2025 Bloomberg ranked him 22nd among the world's most influential pop stars, the only Indian on the list. In 2005 he composed the songs for two films with brief Shah Rukh Khan appearances: Samar Khan's romantic comedy Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye, where Khan appears as himself, and Khalid Mohamed's Silsiilay, which Khan narrates.

name: Samar Khan
career_background: Not documented in the sources consulted; no Wikipedia biography was available.
major_works: Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005); Shaurya (2008)
relationship_with_actor: Directed two films in which Khan contributes briefly: a cameo as himself in Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye and the voice-over narration of Shaurya.
biography: No standalone biography of the director Samar Khan was available; the Wikipedia article under that name is about a different person. This entry rests on the articles for his two films with Shah Rukh Khan, both of which he directed and co-wrote. Kuchh Meetha Ho Jaye (2005), a romantic comedy starring Arshad Warsi and Mahima Chaudhry whose title comes from a Cadbury advertising tagline, features Khan as himself in a cameo. Shaurya (2008), a military courtroom drama produced by Moser Baer and based on the play Court Martial and the film A Few Good Men, features Khan's voice-over narration and was praised for the performances of Kay Kay Menon and Javed Jaffrey.

name: Salim–Sulaiman
career_background: Brothers Salim and Sulaiman Merchant, from a family rooted in Mundra, Kutch; inspired by their father Sadruddin Merchant, who led the Ismaili Scouts Orchestra.
major_works: Kaal (2005); Chak De! India (2007); Neal 'n' Nikki (2005); Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi (2008); Fashion (2008); Love Breakups Zindagi (2011)
recurring_themes: Songs and background scores; Indi-pop and advertising work.
historical_importance: Worked with Yash Chopra, Subhash Ghai and Ram Gopal Varma; Salim Merchant judged Indian Idol season five.
relationship_with_actor: Composed or scored six Khan films, notably the songs of Chak De! India and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi.
biography: Salim–Sulaiman are the brothers Salim and Sulaiman Merchant, whose ancestral town is Mundra in Kutch and who were inspired by their father Sadruddin Merchant, leader of the Ismaili Scouts Orchestra. They composed for Indi-pop acts such as Viva, Aasmaan, Shweta Shetty and Jasmine, produced television commercials, and worked with K. S. Chithra, Zakir Hussain and Sultan Khan before scoring films such as Neal 'n' Nikki, Chak De! India, Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi and Fashion for producers and directors including Yash Chopra, Subhash Ghai and Ram Gopal Varma. Salim Merchant judged the fifth season of Indian Idol. For Shah Rukh Khan they composed songs for the Red Chillies–Dharma horror film Kaal (2005), the songs of Chak De! India (2007) and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi (2008), whose 'Haule Haule' won Sukhwinder Singh a Filmfare Award, and Love Breakups Zindagi (2011). They also wrote the background scores for Heyy Babyy and Bhoothnath.

name: Amol Palekar
career_background: A leading actor of 'middle cinema' in the 1970s; also a painter and author; married to Sandhya Gokhale, who wrote Paheli's screenplay.
major_works: Chhoti Si Baat (1975, actor); Chitchor (1976, actor); Bhumika (1977, actor); Baaton Baaton Mein (1979, actor); Gol Maal (1979, actor); Paheli (2005, director)
recurring_themes: Understated, middle-class storytelling; Paheli adapts a Rajasthani folk tale about desire and duty.
creative_style: Folk-tale lyricism in Paheli, narrated by puppets.
major_awards: Three Filmfare Best Actor awards; six Maharashtra State Film Awards as Best Actor
historical_importance: Part of the group of filmmakers who popularised 'middle cinema'; Paheli was India's Academy Award submission.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Paheli, Red Chillies Entertainment's second production, with Khan as both a neglectful merchant's son and the ghost who takes his place.
biography: Amol Palekar, born on 24 November 1944, is an actor, director and producer in Hindi and Marathi cinema, as well as a painter and author. He was part of the movement that popularised 'middle cinema', with popular films including Chhoti Si Baat (1975), Chitchor (1976), Bhumika (1977), Baaton Baaton Mein (1979) and Gol Maal (1979), and he won three Filmfare Awards and six Maharashtra State Film Awards as Best Actor. He directed Paheli (2005), produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment and based on Vijayadan Detha's Rajasthani short story 'Duvidha', with a screenplay by his wife Sandhya Gokhale. Shah Rukh Khan plays both Kishanlal, a merchant's son who leaves his bride on their wedding night, and the ghost who takes his form and wins her love. The film opened the Zimbabwe International Film Festival, screened at Sundance, and was India's official submission to the Academy Awards; Taran Adarsh called it one of the finest films of recent times.

name: Excel Entertainment
function: Production company (founded by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani)
career_background: Founded in 1999 by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani, who is credited as producer on all four of Khan's Excel films; later added a streaming division, Excel Media & Entertainment.
debut: First production: Dil Chahta Hai (2001).
major_works: Dil Chahta Hai (2001); Lakshya (2004); Don (2006); Luck by Chance (2009); Don 2 (2011); Raees (2017); Gully Boy (2019); Inside Edge (2017); Mirzapur (2018); Made in Heaven (2019)
recurring_themes: Contemporary urban stories, genre reinventions and, later, streaming drama.
major_awards: Dil Chahta Hai won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi; Sidhwani won a BAFTA for producing Boong (2025).
historical_importance: One of the first major Indian production companies to move into over-the-top streaming content; Inside Edge was nominated for an International Emmy.
relationship_with_actor: Produced Khan's two Don films, Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (with Khan as himself) and Raees, the last two Khan films co-produced with Red Chillies.
biography: Excel Entertainment was founded in 1999 by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani. Its first production, Akhtar's Dil Chahta Hai (2001), won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi and screened at the International Film Festival of India. The war drama Lakshya (2004) was critically acclaimed but failed commercially, later gaining a cult following. Excel then produced Don (2006), Akhtar's reboot of the 1978 thriller, starring Shah Rukh Khan as the drug lord and his lookalike, and its sequel Don 2 (2011), co-produced with Khan. It also produced Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (2009), in which Khan appears as himself, and co-produced Rahul Dholakia's Raees (2017) with Red Chillies, with Khan as a Gujarat bootlegger. Sidhwani, born in 1973, expanded the company into streaming through Excel Media & Entertainment, with Inside Edge (2017), nominated for an International Emmy, Mirzapur (2018) and Made in Heaven (2019), and won a BAFTA for producing Boong (2025).

name: Farhan Akhtar
function: Director; producer; screenwriter; actor (co-founder of Excel Entertainment)
career_background: Son of the screenwriters Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani; co-founded Excel Entertainment with Ritesh Sidhwani in 1999.
debut: Directorial debut Dil Chahta Hai (2001); acting debut Rock On!! (2008).
major_works: Dil Chahta Hai (2001); Lakshya (2004); Don (2006); Rock On!! (2008); Luck by Chance (2009, lead actor); Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011); Don 2 (2011); Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (2013)
recurring_themes: Urban youth, friendship and stylish genre reinvention.
creative_style: Contemporary, polished filmmaking; his Don films reboot a 1970s classic as twist-driven action thrillers.
major_awards: National Film Awards for Best Hindi Film (Dil Chahta Hai; Rock On!!, as producer); Filmfare Awards for Best Film (Critics) and Best Screenplay (Dil Chahta Hai), Best Male Debut (Rock On!!), Best Film, Best Supporting Actor and Best Dialogue (Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara) and Best Actor (Bhaag Milkha Bhaag)
historical_importance: Dil Chahta Hai became a cult classic for its realistic urban youth; Excel became a major film and streaming producer.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan as Don in both reboot films, co-produced Don 2 with Red Chillies, starred opposite Khan's cameo in Luck by Chance, and co-produced Raees.
biography: Farhan Akhtar, born on 9 January 1974 to the screenwriters Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani, founded Excel Entertainment with Ritesh Sidhwani in 1999. His directorial debut, Dil Chahta Hai (2001), was acclaimed for depicting urban youth realistically, won the National Film Award for Best Hindi Film and two Filmfare Awards, and has become a cult classic. He then directed the war film Lakshya (2004) and Don (2006), a remake of the 1978 Amitabh Bachchan thriller co-written by his father. Shah Rukh Khan played the drug lord Don and his lookalike Vijay, with a final twist revealing that Don had survived. Akhtar made his acting debut in Rock On!! (2008), which won him a second National Film Award as producer and the Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut. He played the struggling actor Vikram in his sister Zoya Akhtar's Luck by Chance (2009), in which Khan appears as himself. Don 2 (2011), co-produced by Akhtar, Sidhwani and Khan, sent Khan's anti-hero to rob a Berlin bank. Akhtar has also starred in Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011) and Bhaag Milkha Bhaag (2013), which won him the Filmfare Award for Best Actor, and co-produced Khan's gangster film Raees (2017).

name: Vishal–Shekhar
career_background: Vishal Dadlani, vocalist of the electronic band Pentagram, and the classically trained singer Shekhar Ravjiani, childhood friends who met again while recording Pyaar Mein Kabhi Kabhi (1999).
debut: First duo work as guest composers on Champion.
major_works: Jhankaar Beats (2003); Dus (2005); Om Shanti Om (2007); Dostana (2008); Ra.One (2011); Chennai Express (2013); Happy New Year (2014); War (2019); Pathaan (2023)
recurring_themes: Electronic dance, pop, hip hop and Sufi-inflected film songs.
major_awards: Asian Film Award for Best Composer (Om Shanti Om); multiple Filmfare Best Music Director nominations
historical_importance: Featured on over 350 film soundtracks, with more than 3 billion YouTube streams and 72 number-one singles.
relationship_with_actor: Composed the songs for eight Khan films, from I See You and Om Shanti Om to Ra.One, Chennai Express, Happy New Year, Fan and Pathaan; Vishal Dadlani appears in Om Shanti Om.
biography: Vishal–Shekhar are Vishal Dadlani, vocalist of the Mumbai electronic band Pentagram, and Shekhar Ravjiani, a trained classical singer. Childhood friends, they met again in the studio while both contributing to Pyaar Mein Kabhi Kabhi (1999) and formed a duo, first working as guest composers on Champion. Their soundtracks include Jhankaar Beats, Dus, Salaam Namaste, Bluffmaster, Tashan, Dostana, Student of the Year, War and Fighter, and they have collaborated with Akon, Imogen Heap and Diplo. They have been featured on over 350 soundtracks and streamed more than 3 billion times on YouTube. They are Shah Rukh Khan's leading composers of the 2000s–2020s: after a song in I See You (2006), they scored Om Shanti Om (2007), which won the Asian Film Award for Best Composer and in which Dadlani appears as a director, followed by Bhoothnath, Ra.One, Chennai Express, Happy New Year, Fan's marketing song and Pathaan (2023). They have also judged Indian Idol and Sa Re Ga Ma Pa.

name: Shimit Amin
career_background: Born in Kampala, raised in Florida; mathematics graduate of the University of Florida who worked on independent films in Miami and California before editing Bhoot (2003) in India.
debut: Ab Tak Chhappan (2004).
major_works: Bhoot (2003, editor); Ab Tak Chhappan (2004); Chak De! India (2007); Rocket Singh: Salesman of the Year (2009)
recurring_themes: Underdogs and institutions: police, sport and corporate life.
creative_style: Restrained, ensemble-driven realism; in Chak De! India the star does not take over the film.
major_awards: Chak De! India won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment and the Filmfare Critics Award for Best Film.
historical_importance: Chak De! India is ranked among the best Hindi sports films and was named one of India's 25 best films of the 21st century by The Hollywood Reporter India.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan as the disgraced hockey player turned coach Kabir Khan in Chak De! India, which won Khan the Filmfare Award for Best Actor.
biography: Shimit Amin was born in 1975 in Kampala, Uganda, and grew up in Florida, where he graduated in mathematics from the University of Florida. He helped organise North Florida's first Asian and Asian American film festival in 1991, then worked on industrial and independent projects in Miami and California. He came to Indian cinema as editor of Bhoot (2003) and made his first film as director, the police thriller Ab Tak Chhappan (2004), a box-office success. His next film, Chak De! India (2007), written by Jaideep Sahni and produced by Aditya Chopra for Yash Raj Films, starred Shah Rukh Khan as Kabir Khan, a Muslim former hockey captain branded a traitor after a loss to Pakistan, who redeems himself by coaching the neglected women's national team to a World Cup. It was a critical and commercial success, winning the National Film Award for Best Popular Film and five Filmfare Awards, including Best Actor for Khan. Amin's third film was Rocket Singh: Salesman of the Year (2009) with Ranbir Kapoor.

name: B. R. Films
function: Production company founded by B. R. Chopra
career_background: Founded in 1955 by the director B. R. Chopra, a former Lahore film journalist whose youngest brother was Yash Chopra.
major_works: Bhoothnath (2008); Bhoothnath Returns (2014, with T-Series Films)
historical_importance: One of the older Bombay production houses, established after Chopra's success with Afsana (1951).
relationship_with_actor: Produced Bhoothnath, with Khan in an extended special appearance as the father of the boy who befriends a ghost, and co-produced its sequel, in which Khan reprises the role in a cameo.
biography: B. R. Films was formed in 1955 by B. R. Chopra. Born on 22 April 1914 in Rahon, Punjab, and educated at the University of the Punjab in Lahore, Chopra worked as a film journalist with the monthly Cine Herald from 1944 until Partition, when he fled Lahore. His first production, Karwat (1948), flopped, but his directorial debut Afsana (1951), with Ashok Kumar in a double role, was a hit, and he followed it with Chandni Chowk (1954) before founding his own company. His youngest brother was the filmmaker Yash Chopra. For Shah Rukh Khan, B. R. Films, with Ravi Chopra credited as producer, made Vivek Sharma's Bhoothnath (2008), an adaptation of The Canterville Ghost in which Khan plays Aditya Sharma, the father of the boy who befriends a ghost played by Amitabh Bachchan. It was declared a semi-hit. The company co-produced the sequel, Bhoothnath Returns (2014), with T-Series Films, with Renu Ravi Chopra among the producers, and Khan reprised Aditya in a cameo. The Wikipedia page for the company could not be retrieved, so this entry relies on the article about its founder.

name: Pritam
career_background: Born into a Bengali musical family; studied geology at Presidency College and sound engineering at FTII; played in the bands Jotugriher Pakhi and Chandrabindoo and composed ad jingles and television title tracks.
debut: Co-composer with Jeet Gannguli on Tere Liye (2001); solo debut Stumped (2003); breakthrough Dhoom (2004).
major_works: Dhoom (2004); Billu (2009); Barfi! (2012); Dilwale (2015); Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (2016); Jab Harry Met Sejal (2017); Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva (2022); Tiger 3 (2023); Dunki (2023)
recurring_themes: Contemporary romantic ballads and dance songs.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction (70th National Film Awards, Brahmāstra); nine Filmfare Awards, including Best Music Director for Brahmāstra
historical_importance: Has composed for over 125 Bollywood films and founded the music-production platform JAM8 in 2016; his work has also faced plagiarism allegations.
relationship_with_actor: Khan's most frequent composer of the 2010s–2020s, with 12 films from Kismat Konnection and Billu to Dilwale, Jab Harry Met Sejal and Dunki.
biography: Pritam Chakraborty, born on 14 June 1971 and known as Pritam, trained in music with his father, graduated in geology from Presidency College and studied sound recording at FTII Pune. He played in bands including Chandrabindoo and composed advertising jingles and television title tracks in Mumbai from 1997. After co-composing Tere Liye (2001) with Jeet Gannguli and debuting solo with Stumped (2003), he broke through with Dhoom (2004). In over two decades he has composed for more than 125 Hindi films and won a National Film Award and nine Filmfare Awards; Barfi! was his first background score, and he founded the music-production platform JAM8 in 2016. His work has also drawn plagiarism allegations. Pritam has worked on 12 Shah Rukh Khan films, more than any other composer: Kismat Konnection, Billu, Dulha Mil Gaya, Always Kabhi Kabhi, Dilwale ('Gerua'), Ae Dil Hai Mushkil, Tubelight, Jab Harry Met Sejal ('Hawayein'), Laal Singh Chaddha, Brahmāstra, Tiger 3 and Dunki. His Brahmāstra songs won him the National Film Award and the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director.

name: Zoya Akhtar
career_background: Daughter of Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani; studied filmmaking at NYU and assisted Mira Nair, Tony Gerber and Dev Benegal.
debut: Directorial debut Luck by Chance (2009).
major_works: Luck by Chance (2009); Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011); Bombay Talkies (2013, segment); Dil Dhadakne Do (2015); Gully Boy (2019); Made in Heaven (2019–2023); Dahaad (2023)
recurring_themes: Privilege, ambition and relationships among urban Indians, including a satire of the film industry.
creative_style: Observational, character-led drama with ensemble casts.
major_awards: Four Filmfare Awards: Best Debut Director (Luck by Chance) and Best Director (Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara, Gully Boy)
historical_importance: Co-founded Tiger Baby Films with Reema Kagti in 2015 and moved successfully into streaming series.
relationship_with_actor: Cast Khan as himself in both her Bollywood satire Luck by Chance, where he warns a rising actor about fame, and in the song for the centenary anthology Bombay Talkies.
biography: Zoya Akhtar, born on 14 October 1972 to Javed Akhtar and Honey Irani, completed a filmmaking diploma at New York University and assisted Mira Nair, Tony Gerber and Dev Benegal before becoming a writer and director. Her debut, Luck by Chance (2009), a satire of the Hindi film industry produced by her brother Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment, won her the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director and wide critical acclaim. More than a dozen stars play themselves in it, including Shah Rukh Khan, who warns Farhan Akhtar's rising actor about fame and urges him to stay close to his old friends. She broke through commercially with Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara (2011), which won her the Filmfare Award for Best Director, and won the award again for Gully Boy (2019). In between she directed Dil Dhadakne Do (2015) and a segment of Bombay Talkies (2013), the anthology celebrating a century of Indian cinema whose closing song features Khan among many stars. She co-founded Tiger Baby Films with Reema Kagti in 2015 and has made the series Made in Heaven and Dahaad.

name: Fox Star Studios
function: Production and distribution studio (now Star Studio18)
career_background: Founded in March 2008 as one of 21st Century Fox and Star India's film companies; acquired by Disney in 2019; now a subsidiary of JioStar, renamed Star Studio18 in August 2025.
major_works: My Name Is Khan (2010); Neerja (2016); Chhichhore (2019); The Zoya Factor (2019)
major_awards: National Film Awards for Best Hindi Feature Film for Neerja and Chhichhore
historical_importance: A major studio producing and distributing films in Hindi and other South Asian languages.
relationship_with_actor: Co-produced and distributed My Name Is Khan and produced The Zoya Factor, which Khan narrates.
biography: Star Studio18, formerly Fox Star Studios and then Star Studios, is an Indian motion-picture production and distribution company founded in March 2008 and now wholly owned by JioStar, the joint venture between Reliance and Disney India. It produces Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and other South Asian language films through acquisitions, co-productions and in-house productions. It passed to Disney in March 2019 with 21st Century Fox's film businesses, and adopted its current name in August 2025. Its in-house productions Neerja and Chhichhore won National Film Awards for Best Hindi Feature Film. For Shah Rukh Khan, Fox Star Studios, with Fox Searchlight Pictures, Dharma Productions and Red Chillies Entertainment, backed Karan Johar's My Name Is Khan (2010), which 20th Century Fox released worldwide and which set overseas records for a Hindi film. The studio also produced the sports romance The Zoya Factor (2019), which Khan narrates and which was a box-office disaster.

name: Amit Trivedi
career_background: Composed for theatre, advertising jingles and independent music before films.
debut: Aamir (2008).
major_works: Aamir (2008); Dev.D (2009); Bombay Talkies (2013); Udta Punjab (2016); Dear Zindagi (2016); Secret Superstar (2017); Manmarziyaan (2018)
recurring_themes: Indie-pop sensibility in film music.
major_awards: National Film Award for Best Music Direction; Filmfare R. D. Burman Award and Best Background Score (55th Filmfare Awards)
historical_importance: A leading independent-minded film composer since the late 2000s.
relationship_with_actor: Composed Bombay Talkies, whose closing song features Khan, and Dear Zindagi.
biography: Amit Trivedi, born on 8 April 1979 in Mumbai, is a composer, singer and lyricist who began with theatre productions, advertising jingles and independent music before his film debut, Aamir (2008). He won the Filmfare R. D. Burman Award for New Music Talent and the Filmfare Award for Best Background Score at the 55th Filmfare Awards, along with a National Film Award for Best Music Direction, and later earned consecutive Filmfare nominations for Udta Punjab (2016), Secret Superstar (2017) and Manmarziyaan (2018). He composed the music for Bombay Talkies (2013), the centenary anthology whose song 'Apna Bombay Talkies' features Shah Rukh Khan among many stars, and for Gauri Shinde's Dear Zindagi (2016), with lyrics mostly by Kausar Munir, in which Khan plays a psychologist.

name: Amar Mohile
career_background: Son of the composer Anil Mohile.
major_works: Chennai Express (2013, score); Dilwale (2015, score)
relationship_with_actor: Wrote the background scores for Rohit Shetty's two Khan films, Chennai Express and Dilwale.
biography: Amar Mohile is an Indian film-score composer working mainly in Hindi films and the son of the composer Anil Mohile. His Wikipedia article gives little biographical detail beyond a discography. In Shah Rukh Khan's films he is credited with the background scores of Rohit Shetty's action comedies Chennai Express (2013), whose songs were by Vishal–Shekhar, and Dilwale (2015), whose songs were by Pritam.

name: Rohit Shetty
function: Director; producer; stunt director (Rohit Shetty Productions)
career_background: Son of the stuntman M. B. Shetty; began as a stuntman before directing.
debut: Zameen (2003); breakthrough with Golmaal (2006).
major_works: Zameen (2003); Golmaal series (2006–2017); Singham (2011); Bol Bachchan (2012); Chennai Express (2013); Singham Returns (2014); Dilwale (2015); Simmba (2018); Sooryavanshi (2021)
recurring_themes: Action comedy, masala spectacle, car stunts and his 'Cop Universe' franchise.
creative_style: High-energy commercial entertainment with elaborate vehicle stunts.
historical_importance: One of the most commercially successful directors of the 2010s; Chennai Express became the highest-grossing Hindi film at the time.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Khan's two action comedies, Chennai Express and Dilwale, the second co-produced by Shetty with Red Chillies Entertainment.
biography: Rohit Shetty, born on 14 March 1974 and the son of the stuntman M. B. Shetty, is a director, producer and stuntman whose films mix action comedy with masala spectacle. After his debut thriller Zameen (2003) he broke through with the comedy Golmaal (2006), whose sequels each ranked among the highest-grossing films of their years, and he built the Cop Universe with Singham (2011), Singham Returns (2014), Simmba (2018) and Sooryavanshi (2021). His other hits include All the Best (2009) and Bol Bachchan (2012). He has hosted the stunt show Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi since 2014. With Shah Rukh Khan he made Chennai Express (2013), an action comedy in which Khan's reluctant hero helps a crime boss's daughter escape a forced marriage; it opens with a spoof of the train scene from Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge and became, at the time, the highest-grossing Hindi film ever. Shetty then co-produced and directed Dilwale (2015), reuniting Khan and Kajol as lovers torn apart by warring gangster fathers. Critics praised the stars' chemistry but not the screenplay; the film was nonetheless a commercial success.

name: Ram Sampath
career_background: Began composing advertising jingles in Mumbai for brands including Airtel, Docomo, Thums Up and Pepsi; composed pop albums such as Shaan's Tanha Dil (2000); married to the singer Sona Mohapatra.
major_works: Tanha Dil (2000); Khakee (2004); Delhi Belly (2011); Talaash (2012); Bhoothnath Returns (2014); Raees (2017)
major_awards: Filmfare nomination
relationship_with_actor: Contributed songs to Bhoothnath Returns and composed Raees, whose soundtrack drew over 1.6 billion YouTube streams.
biography: Ram Sampath, born on 25 July 1977, is a composer, music producer and musician who started out writing advertising jingles in Mumbai for brands such as Airtel, Docomo, Thums Up, Pepsi and The Times of India. He moved on to pop albums, including Shaan's Tanha Dil (2000), and then to films such as Khakee, Delhi Belly (2011) and Talaash (2012). He is married to the singer Sona Mohapatra. For Shah Rukh Khan's films he was one of the composers of Bhoothnath Returns (2014) and composed Raees (2017) with JAM8; the Raees article reports that its soundtrack received over 1.6 billion streams on YouTube.

name: Maneesh Sharma
career_background: Grew up in Delhi, studied English literature at Hansraj College and filmmaking at the California Institute of the Arts; assistant director at Yash Raj Films on Fanaa, Aaja Nachle and Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi.
debut: Band Baaja Baaraat (2010).
major_works: Band Baaja Baaraat (2010); Ladies vs Ricky Bahl (2011); Shuddh Desi Romance (2013); Fan (2016); Tiger 3 (2023)
recurring_themes: Contemporary romance in his early films; stardom and obsession in Fan; spy action in Tiger 3.
creative_style: Grounded, character-focused filmmaking within the Yash Raj Films system.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director (Band Baaja Baaraat)
historical_importance: A Yash Raj Films director who directed a Khan double role and an instalment of the YRF Spy Universe.
relationship_with_actor: Worked as an assistant on Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi, directed Khan's double role as a star and his obsessive fan in Fan, and gave him a cameo as Pathaan in Tiger 3.
biography: Maneesh Sharma was born on 6 January 1978 in Delhi, where he attended Delhi Public School, R. K. Puram, and studied English literature at Hansraj College. He trained in filmmaking at the California Institute of the Arts and, after returning to India, worked as an assistant director on Yash Raj Films productions including Fanaa (2006), Aaja Nachle (2007) and Shah Rukh Khan's Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi (2008). His debut, Band Baaja Baaraat (2010), with Ranveer Singh and Anushka Sharma, won him the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director; he followed it with Ladies vs Ricky Bahl (2011) and Shuddh Desi Romance (2013). Sharma had conceived Fan in 2006, and Yash Chopra narrated it to Khan that year; the project was revived in late 2013. In the songless thriller (2016) Khan plays both the superstar Aryan Khanna and his obsessive lookalike fan Gaurav, and critics praised the double performance. Sharma's article describes the film as a box-office failure, although it did well overseas. He later directed Tiger 3 (2023), in which Khan appears as Pathaan in a cameo that helps Salman Khan's Tiger escape.

name: Gauri Shinde
career_background: Grew up in Pune and studied at the Symbiosis Institute of Mass Communication; made over 100 advertising and short films, working at agencies including Lowe Lintas under R. Balki, whom she married in 2007.
debut: English Vinglish (2012).
major_works: Oh Man! (2001, short); English Vinglish (2012); Dear Zindagi (2016)
recurring_themes: Women's self-worth and emotional growth.
creative_style: Gentle, conversational character drama.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director (English Vinglish); Laadli National Media Award for Gender Sensitivity
historical_importance: Named in the Financial Times' 2012 list of '25 Indians To Watch'.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote, directed and co-produced Dear Zindagi, casting Khan as the psychologist Jug opposite Alia Bhatt, with Red Chillies Entertainment as co-producer.
biography: Gauri Shinde, born on 6 July 1974, grew up in Pune and graduated from the Symbiosis Institute of Mass Communication. She interned with the documentary director Siddharth Kak and worked in advertising at agencies including Lowe Lintas, where R. Balki, whom she married in 2007, was creative director. She made over 100 advertising films and short films; her short Oh Man! (2001) was selected for the Berlin Film Festival. Her feature debut, English Vinglish (2012), inspired by her mother and marking Sridevi's comeback, premiered at Toronto and was a critical and commercial success, winning her the Filmfare Award for Best Debut Director. She wrote and directed Dear Zindagi (2016), co-produced by her Hope Productions with Red Chillies Entertainment and Dharma Productions. Alia Bhatt plays Kaira, a young cinematographer, and Shah Rukh Khan plays Dr. Jehangir 'Jug' Khan, the free-spirited psychologist who helps her confront her fear of abandonment and gently declines her romantic feelings. The film was a commercial success, and reviewers praised the chemistry between its two leads.

name: Imtiaz Ali
debut: Socha Na Tha (2005).
major_works: Socha Na Tha (2005); Jab We Met (2007); Love Aaj Kal (2009); Rockstar (2011); Highway (2014); Tamasha (2015); Jab Harry Met Sejal (2017); Amar Singh Chamkila (2024); Main Vaapas Aaunga (2026)
recurring_themes: Romance, restlessness, travel and self-discovery.
creative_style: Road-movie romances centred on characters seeking themselves.
major_awards: Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue; several Filmfare Best Director nominations
historical_importance: One of the defining romance filmmakers of 2000s–2010s Hindi cinema.
relationship_with_actor: Wrote and directed Jab Harry Met Sejal, casting Khan as a lonely Punjabi tour guide in Europe opposite Anushka Sharma; Ali later called it a missed opportunity.
biography: Imtiaz Ali, born on 16 June 1971, is a filmmaker best known for writing and directing the romantic comedies Socha Na Tha (2005), Jab We Met (2007) and Love Aaj Kal (2009), and the dramas Rockstar (2011), Highway (2014) and Tamasha (2015); his later work includes Amar Singh Chamkila (2024) and Main Vaapas Aaunga (2026). His films have earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Dialogue and several Best Director nominations. His article marks Jab Harry Met Sejal (2017) as the start of a commercial decline. In that film Shah Rukh Khan plays Harry, a womanising, homesick tour guide in Europe who reluctantly helps a Gujarati tourist (Anushka Sharma) search for her lost engagement ring and falls in love with her. The film was shot across Prague, Amsterdam, Vienna, Lisbon and Budapest and did well overseas, but received mixed-to-negative reviews. Anupama Chopra argued that Ali could not fit Khan's chaste romantic persona to his own 'more bruised brand of romance'. Ali later rated the film 3 out of 10 and called it a missed opportunity.

name: Aanand L. Rai
major_works: Tanu Weds Manu (2011); Raanjhanaa (2013); Tanu Weds Manu Returns (2015); Zero (2018); Atrangi Re (2021); Raksha Bandhan (2022)
recurring_themes: Small-town romance and relationships.
creative_style: Romantic comedy-drama rooted in north Indian settings.
major_awards: Filmfare Best Director nominations for Raanjhanaa and Tanu Weds Manu Returns
historical_importance: A successful director of small-town romances whose big-budget Zero is marked in his article as the start of a career decline.
relationship_with_actor: Directed and co-produced Zero, in which Khan plays a man with dwarfism torn between a scientist with cerebral palsy and a film star.
biography: Aanand L. Rai is a director and producer known for the romantic comedy-dramas Tanu Weds Manu (2011) and Tanu Weds Manu Returns (2015) and the romantic drama Raanjhanaa (2013), the last two of which earned him Filmfare nominations for Best Director. He then directed the big-budget romantic drama Zero (2018), produced by his Colour Yellow Productions with Red Chillies Entertainment, followed by Atrangi Re (2021) and Raksha Bandhan (2022). In Zero, Shah Rukh Khan plays Bauua Singh, a brash man with dwarfism from Meerut who abandons a scientist with cerebral palsy (Anushka Sharma), is drawn into a film star's world (Katrina Kaif), and tries to redeem himself by volunteering for a mission to Mars. Critics praised the visual effects and the performances but found the second half overwrought, and the film was highly unsuccessful at the box office. Rai's article heads this period 'Career decline (2018–present)'.

name: Tanuj Tiku
career_background: Not documented; no Wikipedia biography was available.
major_works: Laal Singh Chaddha (2022, score); Tiger 3 (2023, score)

biography: No standalone biography of Tanuj Tiku was available. The film articles credit him with the background scores of Laal Singh Chaddha (2022), Aamir Khan's remake of Forrest Gump, in which Shah Rukh Khan appears as his younger self, and Tiger 3 (2023), in which Khan appears as Pathaan. Pritam wrote the songs for both films.

name: Siddharth Anand
career_background: Grandson of the screenwriter Inder Raj Anand.
major_works: Salaam Namaste (2005); Ta Ra Rum Pum (2007); Bachna Ae Haseeno (2008); Anjaana Anjaani (2010); Bang Bang! (2014); War (2019); Pathaan (2023); Fighter (2024)
recurring_themes: Romantic comedy early on, then large-scale action and spy thrillers.
creative_style: Glossy, star-driven action spectacle.
historical_importance: Pathaan launched the crossover YRF Spy Universe and ranks among the highest-grossing Hindi films.
relationship_with_actor: Directed Pathaan, which gave Khan his biggest commercial comeback, and is directing and producing King, Khan's next film, with his daughter Suhana Khan.
biography: Siddharth Anand, the grandson of the screenwriter Inder Raj Anand, first gained recognition for romantic comedies such as Salaam Namaste (2005), Ta Ra Rum Pum (2007), Bachna Ae Haseeno (2008) and Anjaana Anjaani (2010), before turning to action with Bang Bang! (2014), War (2019) and Pathaan (2023). In 2021 he launched his production company Marflix Pictures, whose first release was Fighter (2024). Pathaan, produced by Aditya Chopra for Yash Raj Films, cast Shah Rukh Khan as an exiled RAW agent who stops a former colleague's plot to release a virus on India. It established crossovers in the YRF Spy Universe and broke box-office records, becoming the first Hindi film to gross ₹100 crore worldwide on its opening day. Anand's next project is King, which he is directing and producing with Khan, Suhana Khan in her theatrical debut, and Abhishek Bachchan; it is scheduled for release after the research cutoff.

name: Atlee
debut: Raja Rani (2013).
major_works: Raja Rani (2013); Theri (2016); Mersal (2017); Bigil (2019); Jawan (2023)
recurring_themes: Mass-appeal action dramas with social messages.
creative_style: High-octane commercial Tamil filmmaking with plot twists and star-centred set pieces.
major_awards: Vijay Award for Best Debut Director and Tamil Nadu State Award for Best Dialogue (Raja Rani)
historical_importance: His Hindi debut, Jawan, is among the highest-grossing Indian films; his work has also faced plagiarism allegations.
relationship_with_actor: Directed and co-wrote Jawan, casting Khan in a double role as a vigilante jailer and his wrongly disgraced father; Khan had described Atlee's Bigil as 'Chak De India on steroids'.
biography: Arun 'Atlee' Kumar, born on 21 September 1986, is a filmmaker working primarily in Tamil cinema. His debut, Raja Rani (2013), won him the Vijay Award for Best Debut Director and the Tamil Nadu State Award for best dialogue, and he followed it with three hits starring Vijay: Theri (2016), Mersal (2017) and Bigil (2019), which Shah Rukh Khan described as 'Chak De India on steroids'. His films have also attracted plagiarism allegations. Atlee made his Hindi debut with Jawan (2023), produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment. Khan plays Azad, a prison jailer who leads a band of women inmates in heists exposing corruption, and his father Vikram, a soldier framed by an arms dealer. The film broke opening-day records, overtook Pathaan as the highest net-grossing Hindi film in India, and won Khan the National Film Award for Best Actor. Critics credited Khan's screen image with selling its conceit, although some found the story chaotic.

name: Rajkumar Hirani
function: Director; producer; screenwriter; editor (Rajkumar Hirani Films)
career_background: Worked as a film editor and on advertising films; his first film as a professional editor was Mission Kashmir (2000).
debut: Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003).
major_works: Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003); Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006); 3 Idiots (2009); PK (2014); Dunki (2023)
recurring_themes: Light-hearted films about significant social issues.
creative_style: Humour combined with emotional intelligence.
major_awards: Four National Film Awards and eleven Filmfare Awards for his films
historical_importance: 3 Idiots was the highest-grossing Indian film of its time.
relationship_with_actor: Co-wrote, co-produced and directed Dunki, their first film together, casting Khan as an ex-soldier leading villagers on an illegal migration route to England.
biography: Rajkumar 'Raju' Hirani, born on 20 November 1962, began as a film editor and advertising filmmaker; his first feature as a professional editor was Vidhu Vinod Chopra's Mission Kashmir (2000). His directorial debut, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003), was a critical and commercial success that won the Filmfare Award for Best Film (Critics) and brought Hirani the Filmfare Award for Best Screenplay. Its sequel Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006) was the second-highest grosser of its year, and both won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film. His coming-of-age comedy 3 Idiots (2009) became the highest-grossing Indian film of its time, and he followed it with the religious satire PK (2014). His films are known for treating serious social issues with humour and have won four National Film Awards and eleven Filmfare Awards. Hirani co-wrote, co-produced, edited and directed Dunki (2023) with Jio Studios and Red Chillies Entertainment. Shah Rukh Khan plays Hardy, an ex-soldier who leads villagers from Punjab to England on the illegal 'donkey flight' route and returns 25 years later to bring home the dying woman he loves. The film received mixed reviews but was one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of 2023.
